column1: # Browser-REPL transcript expectations for the WASM `repl_eval` surface.
# Consumed by scripts/run_wasm_differential.sh (drives scripts/lib/
# wasm_repl_runner.js).  This gates the entry point the website's REPL and
# every runnable docs code block call — `repl_eval` — which the batch
# execute-and-diff sweep never touches, because that sweep drives
# `run_program`.
# WHAT IS BEING ASSERTED
# Emscripten hands stdout to the embedder's `print` callback one COMPLETE
# LINE at a time (site/static/index.html accumulates `text + '\n'` per call).
# So a REPL answer only reaches the page if it is newline-TERMINATED, and the
# expected column below is the list of finished lines the page receives — not
# "the characters the VM wrote".  An answer that loses its terminator shows up
# here as an empty transcript, which is exactly what the browser shows.
# The cases run IN ORDER against ONE persistent session: definitions made by
# an earlier row must still be in scope in a later one, so the session's
# persistence is under test too.
# Columns (TAB-separated):
#   1  expression   Eshkol source handed to repl_eval() verbatim
#   2  transcript   expected complete lines, joined by the two characters
#                   \ and n; EMPTY means the page receives nothing
#   3  note         why this row is here

column3: auto-print of a value answer is one terminated line

column1: (define (sq x) (* x x))
column3: a definition is not an answer — no transcript line
the definition from the previous eval is still in scope

column1: (string-append "eshkol" "-" "repl")
column3: string answers print in display syntax, unquoted

column1: (apply vector (list 1 2 3))
column3: apply + vector answer round-trips through the echo

column1: (map (lambda (x) (* 2 x)) (list 1 2 3))
column3: stdlib higher-order call through the persistent session

column1: (display "hi")
column3: display writes a FRAGMENT — no terminator, so no line yet

column1: (newline)
column3: the pending "hi" fragment completes into a line here

column1: (begin (display "a") (newline) 7)
column3: explicit output line, then the auto-printed answer line
